reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Reuters: coalition reports 13 civilians wounded in renewed Houthi attacks
reports.text: The retrieved opening of the September 15 Reuters report says the Houthis claimed Monday missile and drone attacks on the Khamis Mushait airbase. Reuters attributes 13 civilian injuries in the attacks to the Saudi-led coalition and reports emergency alerts in Khamis Mushait and three other southern cities. The remainder of the article and the underlying coalition statement were not retrieved. Military target damage and civilian injuries are not independently verified. This is newly reviewed reporting of September 14 attacks, not a newly verified attack within this scan.
reports.implication: The coalition-attributed injury report describes civilian consequences of renewed attacks; claimed damage to the airbase remains unverified.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Zelenskyy conditions energy-strike pause on credible Russian restraint
reports.text: Reuters and POLITICO report September 14 statements in which Zelenskyy offers reciprocal restraint if partners secure genuine Russian willingness to stop attacks on Ukrainian energy and critical infrastructure. Trump separately claimed an agreement; the retrieved reporting does not establish an implemented mutual ceasefire. The official social-media statement could not be read directly. The outlets share attribution to presidential statements, not independent verification of a cessation. Newly reviewed earlier reporting, not a new attack in this scan.
reports.implication: Ukraine’s offer is conditional; the statements do not establish an implemented mutual halt to energy strikes.
reports.next_trigger: Zelenskyy says Ukraine awaits specifics from partners on a reliable, long-term arrangement.

reports.headline: ArcelorMittal reports fatal missile strike and halted primary steel production
reports.text: Reuters reports on September 14 that ArcelorMittal says a September 12 ballistic missile strike killed two contractors and injured two employees at Kryvyi Rih. The company statement distributed via GlobeNewswire and carried by FinancialContent says ironmaking complex #1 was hit, primary steel production is halted, and other facilities are idled or operating minimally. Both full texts were reviewed; Reuters shares company attribution and does not independently verify the attack. Exact attack time and restoration date remain unknown. This is newly reviewed reporting of a September 12 event, not a new attack in the three-hour scan window.
reports.implication: The company reports halted primary steel production while damage and repairs are assessed; the restart date remains unknown.
reports.next_trigger: The company says further operational updates will follow completed damage assessments and clearer repair timelines.

reports.headline: Reuters: Iranian strait authority lists 77 vessels for threatened passage restrictions
reports.text: Reuters attributes an updated list of 77 vessels to Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority on Monday. The body says listed vessels face future passage restrictions including fines, detention or confiscation; cooperating vessels could be added and insurers/P&I clubs/classification societies are warned against providing services. This is an attributed policy announcement, not verified enforcement, seizure or closure. The original X post and vessel list were not retrieved. No independent confirmation or explicit next trigger established.
reports.implication: The reported list threatens future passage restrictions, fines, detention or confiscation; it does not establish that any listed vessel has been seized or the strait closed.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Oman postpones Salalah regional meeting to a later date
reports.text: Oman Foreign Ministry publication dated September 13 says the regional meeting scheduled for Monday in Salalah is postponed to a later date to create conditions for constructive dialogue. The ministry-hosted English text is identified as an unofficial translation of its Arabic report. Reuters also attributes postponement to the foreign minister; this is shared official attribution, not independent verification. No replacement date is supplied. This is newly reviewed reporting, not a new attack during this scan.
reports.implication: The planned regional dialogue will not take place on Monday as scheduled; the notice does not establish an end to diplomacy or any change in shipping access.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: UKMTO update reports fire and crew evacuation after Hormuz vessel strike
reports.text: Anadolu and Middle East Eye report a UKMTO update describing fire aboard the previously reported Hormuz vessel and local authorities assisting crew evacuation. Both full reports were reviewed. They share UKMTO attribution and are not independent verification. Middle East Eye identifies Warning 134-26 Update 001 and publishes at 10:49 BST on September 13. Anadolu says UKMTO received the initial report at 23:00 UTC on September 12; this is a report-receipt time, not the strike time. The underlying bulletin was not retrieved from the official website. Exact strike time, vessel identity, casualties, damage extent and environmental effects remain unknown. The separately reported Hengam/Qeshm casualties cannot safely be identified as this incident. This revises the existing incident rather than establishing a new attack in this scan.
reports.implication: The reported fire and evacuation extend the known consequences of the retained vessel strike; casualty totals, damage extent and responsibility remain unverified.
reports.next_trigger: UKMTO says an investigation is underway; its findings remain pending.
reports.material_revision: UKMTO update reports an onboard fire and local authorities assisting crew evacuation.

reports.headline: UKMTO reports vessel struck by unidentified projectile in Hormuz
reports.text: Anadolu reports a September 13 UKMTO statement that a vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unidentified munition. Crew condition, damage and environmental impact were unknown; an investigation was underway. The full Anadolu article was reviewed. Retrieved Reuters/AFP reporting carried by RTE also attributes a projectile report to UKMTO, but shares the same official attribution and is not independent confirmation. The underlying UKMTO notice was not retrieved. No vessel name or exact event time is established. A separate Iranian report of casualties near Qeshm cannot safely be identified as this same incident. This is newly reviewed reporting, not a verified attack within the three-hour scan window.
reports.implication: The attributed notice identifies a reported strike on commercial shipping; casualties, damage, responsibility and any effect on passage remain unverified.
reports.next_trigger: UKMTO says an investigation is underway; its findings remain pending.

reports.headline: Rosatom chief alleges September 11 attack on Zaporizhzhia diesel deliveries
reports.text: Reuters and TASS report on September 13 that Rosatom chief Alexei Likhachev accused Ukraine of September 11 strikes on diesel fuel trucks near the Zaporizhzhia plant perimeter, killing two Russian servicemen and injuring others. TASS quotes the Rosatom statement; Reuters syndication was also read. This is shared official attribution, not independent verification. The original Rosatom-hosted statement was not retrieved. The IAEA September 11 update, read via UN OCHA, separately says restored external power eased blackout risk but depleted diesel reserves need replenishment; it does not verify this attack allegation. This is newly reviewed reporting of an earlier event, not a new attack in this scan.
reports.implication: The allegation concerns fuel deliveries needed for backup cooling power; responsibility, casualties and the effect on plant reserves remain unverified.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: AFP/AP report Lebanon-Israel Rome talks postponed until October
reports.text: AFP and AP reporting carried by Al Jazeera says the September round of US-mediated Rome talks has been postponed until October, citing an unnamed US official. President Aoun said there would be no new negotiations at the moment. The same official said ambassadors would meet at the US State Department next week on the June framework. The full article was reviewed; the underlying official statements were not retrieved. This is attributed reporting, not independent confirmation of a ceasefire or an end to diplomatic contact. Exact event and publication times are unknown.
reports.implication: The reported postponement delays the next Rome round, but planned ambassador-level contact means diplomacy has not been shown to end.
reports.next_trigger: The cited US official says ambassadors will meet at the State Department next week; the meeting and any outcome remain unconfirmed.

reports.headline: South Korea reports short-range North Korean missile launches from Wonsan
reports.text: AFP reporting carried by The Star attributes multiple short-range ballistic missile launches from Wonsan and flights of about 250 km to South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff. It reports that US Pacific Command assessed no immediate threat to US territory or allies. The full report was reviewed; original military statements were not retrieved and launch details are not independently verified. The article describes a prior-day launch, not a newly timed event within this scan. It does not establish a nuclear test or warhead loading.
reports.implication: The reported launches follow trilateral exercises; the cited US assessment does not identify an immediate threat to US territory or allies.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Saudi Civil Defence reports two wounded by projectile in Al-Tuwal
reports.text: Al Jazeera reports Saudi Civil Defence said a Houthi projectile landed in Al-Tuwal, Jazan, on Saturday, wounding two people and damaging a mosque, buildings and vehicles. The original reporting was read in full; the underlying Saudi statement was not retrieved, and the casualties and attribution remain unverified. Exact event and publication times are unknown. A separate Houthi claim concerning Sharurah in Najran is not independent confirmation of this Jazan incident. This is newly reviewed reporting of a prior-day event, not a verified attack in the current three-hour window.
reports.implication: The attributed report describes civilian injuries and property damage in Al-Tuwal; it does not independently establish the separate claimed Sharurah base strike.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Iraq reportedly dismisses Maysan commander after Saudi pipeline drone attack
reports.text: BBC September 12 reporting and Reuters reporting republished by The Straits Times attribute to the Iraqi prime ministers office acknowledgement that the pipeline drones originated in Maysan and dismissal of its operations commander. These accounts cite the same official statement, which was not retrieved directly; they do not independently verify launch origin or identify those responsible. This is a revision of the retained September 10 pipeline attack, not a new attack within this scan. Saudi restraint and the investigation were already retained. Exact publication and dismissal times and pipeline restart status remain unknown.
reports.implication: Reported Iraqi acknowledgement and a command dismissal extend the response to the existing pipeline attack; responsibility for launching the drones remains unresolved.
reports.next_trigger: Iraq says an investigation into the attack and those responsible has been ordered.
reports.material_revision: Iraq reportedly acknowledges launch territory and dismisses the Maysan operations commander.

reports.headline: The National: preliminary tracking counted 15 Bab al-Mandeb crossings on September 11
reports.text: The National reports preliminary Kpler data showing 15 ship crossings on September 11, compared with 30 on September 10; six exited the Red Sea and nine entered. Its original report was read in full. The underlying Kpler dataset was not retrieved and the count is not independently verified. This is newly reviewed reporting on a prior-day traffic window, not a newly timed attack or proof of a shipping closure. The same report gives 14 Hormuz crossings on September 11, compared with seven on September 10; the two waterways are not interchangeable.
reports.implication: The reported traffic decline indicates fewer crossings, not a complete closure of Bab al-Mandeb; the preliminary count remains unverified.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Odesa residential damage and injuries reported after overnight Russian attack
reports.text: Odesa governor Oleh Kiper reported 28 injured, including two children, in a public September 12 post at 07:41:48 UTC. Kyiv Independent and Euronews report residential-building damage and at least 35 injured in Odesa Oblast, citing local authorities. The directly retrieved governor post still gives 28; the primary publication supporting 35 was not retrieved. These accounts share official attribution and do not independently verify the casualty total. The attack occurred overnight before this scan; exact event time remains unknown. Newly reviewed reporting is not a newly timed attack in this three-hour window.
reports.implication: Reported damage to a residential building and injuries show civilian harm in Odesa; the casualty count remains attributed and subject to revision.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Mandalay airport closure reported after September 10 drone attack
reports.text: DVB September 11 reporting attributes a September 10-12 airport closure and September 11 flight cancellations to authorities and airlines after a drone attack at Tada-U air base. AP reporting carried by DVB quotes an NUG spokesman claiming the attack and regime media acknowledging drones but denying damage. Aircraft-loss and casualty claims are not independently verified. This is newly reviewed reporting on a September 10 event, not a new attack within this scan. Original airline and military statements were not retrieved.
reports.implication: Reported flight cancellations show civilian transport disruption; damage and casualty claims remain unverified.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Saudi Arabia attributes pipeline drones to Iraq and holds off retaliation
reports.text: Reuters reports a September 11 Saudi foreign ministry statement attributing the East-West pipeline drones to launches from Iraq. Riyadh says it will not retaliate for now following the Iraqi prime ministers request, while reserving its right to protect its interests. Al Jazeera/AFP quotes the same Saudi statement and an Iraqi statement ordering an investigation; these are attributed official accounts, not independent verification of the launch origin. This revises the existing September 10 attack report, not a newly timed attack. The pipeline restart time remains unknown.
reports.implication: Saudi Arabia links the existing attack to launches from Iraq but says it is withholding retaliation for now; launch origin remains an official attribution.
reports.next_trigger: Iraq says an investigation into the attack and those responsible has been ordered.
reports.material_revision: Saudi attribution of launch territory and announced restraint add material diplomatic context to the existing pipeline attack.

reports.headline: Saudi ministry reports temporary East-West pipeline shutdown after attacks
reports.text: Reuters on September 11 at 20:08 UTC reports, citing Saudi state media and an energy ministry source, that the East-West pipeline was temporarily shut after several attacks in Riyadh and Medina on Thursday. Some people were injured and received treatment. The official SPA page title matches the shutdown claim, but its full statement could not be retrieved. This is newly reviewed reporting, not a newly timed attack in this scan. Responsibility, restart time and independent verification are not established.
reports.implication: The reported shutdown interrupts a Saudi oil transport route; the duration and restart status are not established by the retrieved report.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: IAEA: restored Zaporizhzhia power eases blackout risk, but diesel reserves need replenishment
reports.text: September 11 IAEA Update 366, read in full through its ReliefWeb republication, confirms the September 7 evening reconnection already reported. It adds that depleted diesel reserves must be replenished before another external-power cut; resupply remains difficult and off-site fuel storage is reportedly empty. This is a material follow-up to the existing restoration report, not a new blackout. Anadolu reports the same IAEA statement and is not independent verification of fuel stocks.
reports.originating_source: IAEA; full statement republished by ReliefWeb
reports.implication: Restored power has eased immediate blackout risk, but depleted diesel reserves leave the plant vulnerable to another external-power cut.
reports.next_trigger: IAEA calls for diesel replenishment before any further external-power cut.
reports.material_revision: IAEA details depleted diesel reserves and difficult resupply after power restoration.

reports.headline: Houthis reportedly take Perim island at the entrance to the Red Sea
reports.text: BBC cites an official and eyewitness speaking to AFP on Friday. AP separately quotes a Yemeni government military official and a Houthi official, both anonymous, confirming the Mayun island seizure. Guardian also reports the takeover. Reporting establishes attributed accounts, not independently inspected territorial control. Exact event time is unavailable; no verified closure of Bab al-Mandab is established.
reports.implication: Reported control of Perim strengthens the Houthis’ position at Bab al-Mandab, a key Saudi oil export route; it does not establish a shipping closure.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Reuters: preliminary tracking counted seven Hormuz transits on September 10
reports.text: Reuters reports preliminary Kpler data showed seven transits on September 10 versus 11 the prior day and a 10-day average of 15. Two vessels exited and five entered. Data as of 03:06 GMT on September 11 excludes vessels with AIS transponders off. Direct Kpler dataset was not retrieved; counts remain attributed.
reports.implication: The reported traffic decline is not zero traffic and does not verify the IRGC claim that Hormuz is closed.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: IRGC says it struck a US unmanned surface vessel at the entrance to Hormuz
reports.text: CGTN reports the IRGC said on Thursday it struck a Saildrone Explorer-type unmanned surface vessel at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. Al Jazeera repeats the IRGC claim. Both rely on the same party claim; this review does not establish damage or independent confirmation. The IRGC closure assertion is not verified traffic data.
sources: CGTN with Xinhua input, quoting IRGC
reports.implication: The reported targeting concerns an unmanned vessel; damage and the claimed closure of Hormuz are not independently established.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Zelenskiy says no trilateral peace meeting before Russia’s September 20 elections
reports.text: Reuters quotes Zelenskiy on September 10 saying no trilateral meeting on ending the war will occur before Russian elections on September 20. He hopes for progress on energy and grain talks late in September following a meeting with Trump. The anticipated progress is not an agreement or observed ceasefire. No independently retrieved presidential transcript corroborated this scan.
reports.originating_source: Volodymyr Zelenskiy quoted by Reuters
reports.implication: The reported timetable rules out a trilateral meeting before September 20; continuing contacts do not establish a ceasefire.
reports.next_trigger: Zelenskiy anticipates energy and grain talks late in September; any resulting agreement remains unconfirmed.

reports.headline: August 28 IAEA report identifies additional Yongbyon enrichment facility; newly reviewed, not a new test
reports.text: The August 28 report identifies Yongbyon UEF2 using June visit photographs and satellite imagery, and says the building could accommodate up to 28 depicted cascades. It records indications of Kangson annex operations beginning in January 2026. Paragraph 13 explicitly says the Agency cannot confirm operational status or configuration without access; inspectors have been absent since 2009. Reuters via CNN repeats the same assessment, not independent site verification. Newly reviewed historical capacity evidence, not a September 10 commissioning or nuclear test.
sources: IAEA Director General report dated August 28
Reuters via CNN citing the same IAEA report
reports.originating_source: IAEA
reports.implication: The IAEA assessment indicates expanded enrichment capacity; without on-site access it cannot confirm facility operations or configuration.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Houthis reportedly capture Mocha; government sources and residents describe takeover
reports.text: Reuters attributes Mocha capture to four Yemeni government military sources. BBC Arabic resident interviews describe Houthi patrols after Wednesday-night fighting. CNN quotes the information minister confirming capture. Newly reviewed September 10 reporting, not established as a new event in this three-hour window. Exact revision time and direct official publication remain unavailable. Hanish and Perim claims are not independently verified here.
reports.implication: Reported control of this Red Sea port strengthens the Houthis’ position near Bab el-Mandeb; it does not establish closure of the strait.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: BBC reports IAEA board adopted Iran UN referral, superseding draft-only status
reports.text: BBC reports the IAEA board passed the UK-France-Germany-US resolution, with 23 votes in favour, eight abstentions and China, Russia and Niger opposed. This updates the September 8 draft-only account; that earlier account is retained as dated history. The IAEA resolutions page retrieved in this scan lists June 10 as its latest 2026 resolution and did not supply the adopted September text. This is attributed reporting, not a fresh enrichment measurement, automatic sanctions or independently verified military escalation.
reports.originating_source: BBC Persian and BBC reporting
reports.implication: The reported decision advances referral beyond a draft; it does not itself establish new sanctions or a nuclear-weapons development.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Sarmada weapons-depot explosion: Syrian authorities report 14 dead in preliminary toll
reports.text: SANA reports a September 9 explosion at a weapons depot in Burj Elnumra near Sarmada, citing local health and emergency officials. Its earlier toll was three killed and ten injured. DW, credited with AFP, AP and Reuters, reports the Idlib health department’s preliminary toll of 14 killed and 11 injured and says the cause has not been announced. These are attributed, evolving counts rather than independent casualty verification. This is distinct from the September 1 Binnish ammunition-vehicle explosion.
sources: DW with AFP, AP, Reuters citing Idlib health department
reports.originating_source: Idlib Health Directorate and emergency official via SANA
reports.implication: Secondary explosions and fires hampered rescue efforts; the cause remains unannounced, so this is not established as a new attack.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Jordan reports intercepting 18 of 20 Iranian missiles; no casualties reported
reports.text: Petra carries the JAF statement that air defences engaged 20 ballistic missiles from Iranian territory, intercepting 18; two fell in unpopulated areas and no casualties were recorded. Reuters attributes an Al Azraq base attack to the IRGC and reports a US official described strikes as ineffective. Iranian heavy-damage claims are not independently verified. Counts and outcomes remain attributed. This September 9 attack is distinct from earlier Larak-related attacks and the September 8 US tanker strikes.
sources: Reuters citing Jordan, Iran and a US official
BBC citing JAF; not independent count verification
reports.originating_source: Jordan Armed Forces statement via Petra
reports.implication: The reported Iranian missile attack extends the latest US-Iran exchange to Jordan; interception and casualty figures remain attributed to Jordanian authorities.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: CENTCOM reports five Iranian tankers struck on September 8
reports.text: CENTCOM states it struck Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1 and Riesco in the Gulf of Oman and Derya near Kharg Island on September 8, after attempted missile attacks on a US warship. It says crews were ordered to abandon ship and vessels rendered inoperable. Reuters reports the same US statement; this is not independent verification of the damage. This is distinct from the three tankers struck on September 5.
sources: Reuters citing CENTCOM (not independent damage verification)
reports.originating_source: U.S. Central Command Public Affairs via DVIDS
reports.implication: The US military reports additional strikes on Iranian oil shipping, distinct from its September 5 operation; damage remains attributed.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: Saudi authorities report 73 civilians injured in Houthi attacks on four southern cities
reports.text: Petra carries the Saudi statement reporting 73 civilians injured in Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on September 8. Anadolu quotes the Energy Ministry reporting fires and temporary operational halts. Reuters via CNA reports satellite smoke observations but says ground images and witnesses were unavailable. The casualty figure remains attributed to Saudi authorities, not independently established here.
reports.originating_source: Saudi statement via Petra / SPA
reports.implication: Reported fires and temporary operational halts affect southern Saudi energy facilities; the casualty total remains attributed.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: AFP revises Umm Rawaba strike toll from 12 to 13 dead; 22 injured
reports.text: AFP reports a hospital source revised the death toll from 12 to 13 after another person died of injuries; 22 injured remain in treatment. RSF responsibility remains attributed, with no immediate RSF comment. This updates the same September 8 strike outside the courthouse, not a separate attack.
sources: AFP via France 24; earlier AFP via Arab News (same agency, not independent confirmation)
reports.originating_source: AFP via France 24
reports.implication: The same courthouse-area attack has a revised reported casualty toll; responsibility remains attributed.
reports.next_trigger: Not supplied by source evidence.

reports.headline: UK commits GBP100 million to Ukraine winter air defence
reports.text: UK Ministry of Defence confirms a GBP100 million PURL contribution including Patriot missiles, with delivery planned before winter. This is military assistance, not a collective-defence invocation.

reports.headline: New Hintalo strike allegation warrants close watch
reports.text: AFP reports a TPLF allegation of a September 8 drone strike; a hospital source reports at least three wounded. AFP could not independently verify the claim, and the federal army had not commented. No confirmed death toll or new activation.

reports.headline: AFP reports deadly strike outside Umm Rawaba courthouse
reports.text: A medical source tells AFP 12 people were killed; witnesses describe a drone striking a tree outside the courthouse. RSF responsibility remains attributed and there was no immediate RSF comment. Do not infer confirmed destruction of the courthouse.

reports.headline: Destroyer commissioning adds nuclear-posture concern
reports.text: Dong-A reports KCNA announced September 6 commissioning of Kang Gun Ho and Kim nuclear-navy remarks. This does not establish actual warhead loading, a new launch or a nuclear explosion. Canonical test flags remain unchanged.

reports.headline: Zaporizhzhia power reconnection gains IAEA-attributed corroboration
reports.text: Interfax-Ukraine attributes September 7 Ferosplavna-1 reconnection to Energoatom and an IAEA statement following locally protected repairs. This improves nuclear safety without establishing a general cessation of hostilities.

reports.headline: Saudi energy fires corroborated; existing signal retained
reports.text: Reuters reports Saudi energy-facility fires and a coalition account of 73 wounded across four southern cities on September 8. Coalition warns of an operational response. Existing facility-attack signal is not counted twice.

reports.headline: Zaporizhzhia grid restoration: stronger sourcing, residual risk
reports.text: Hromadske full September 8 report attributes September 7 restoration of Ferosplavna-1 power to Energoatom. This improves verification beyond prior index-only coverage but is not a directly verified new IAEA restoration statement. New Kyiv strikes reported; localized nuclear-safety repairs do not imply general ceasefire.

reports.headline: Iran repeats exclusion-zone threats; operational extent unverified
reports.text: September 8 Reuters via Geo reports renewed economic-warfare and exclusion-zone threats. Missile use is an Iranian claim referring to prior days; US denies hits. No verified zero traffic or fresh minefield. Historical mining flag retained, not freshly corroborated.

reports.headline: Inspection gap persists; UN referral still a draft
reports.text: September 8 Al Jazeera/Reuters confirms continuing IAEA information/access gap; E3/US referral resolution remains unsubmitted draft. No new weapons-grade enrichment or test verified.

reports.headline: Saudi energy disruption keeps oil risk elevated
reports.text: Saudi-attributed disruption remains an existing signal, not a new activation. Reuters syndication quotes Brent $99.00 and WTI $94.41 at 08:00 UTC; timestamped intraday prices, not live quotes.

reports.headline: Saudi energy sites hit; operational stoppages reported
reports.text: September 8 Al Jazeera full direct report quotes Saudi energy ministry: energy sites hit early Tuesday, fires and temporary operational halts. Houthis subsequently claim a large missile/drone operation. AP also reports Saudi-attributed 73 wounded; Al Jazeera says the coalition did not date that casualty total. Activate infrastructure_strike; do not imply independently audited damage or confirmed territorial gains. Existing score remains saturated.

reports.headline: Newer reports say Zaporizhzhia external power restored
reports.text: September 7 evening Ukrainska Pravda, Energoatom-attributed coverage and an IAEA-attributed headline report restored external electricity. This supersedes an unqualified repairs-pending narrative, but remains index-level in this run; official IAEA feed carries earlier statements and direct statement access is challenged. Grid reliability remains a watch item; retain existing localized repair-arrangement signal.

reports.headline: Iran referral still a draft; verification gap persists
reports.text: September 8 Al Jazeera/Reuters reiterates Iran material-accounting and on-site verification gaps; the E3/US referral draft is not yet formally submitted in that report. No new technical threshold independently established; keep existing access-gap signal.

reports.headline: Iran threatens Gulf energy assets; restricted zone proposed
reports.text: Reuters September 7 full extract confirms conditional Gulf energy threats and a proposed restricted zone; neither establishes zero traffic or a freshly verified minefield. Retain historical mining status with explicit verification caveat; no score increase.

reports.headline: Freedom Edge confirmed; destroyer report is prior context
reports.text: September 6 destroyer commissioning remains prior context; September 7-11 Freedom Edge confirmed by DVIDS. Neither establishes a new configured DPRK test this scan; hold.

reports.headline: Seoul forum confrontation is not a maritime attack
reports.text: New September 8 Korean press headlines cover Philippine defence chief's clash with Chinese delegates at Seoul forum. Diplomatic confrontation is not a verified armed maritime incident; hold.

reports.headline: Iran referral remains draft; inspection gap persists
reports.text: IAEA full September 7 statement confirms no declared-facility information or in-field access during reporting period. September 8 Al Jazeera/Reuters confirms E3/US referral draft is still unsubmitted and wording remains unsettled. No new 90-percent enrichment or nuclear test verified; retain existing access-gap signal.

reports.headline: Zaporizhzhia repair arrangement is not grid restoration
reports.text: HISTORICAL September 7 pre-restoration assessment. Superseded by Energoatom-attributed September 7 evening restoration reported in full by Hromadske on September 8. IAEA September 7 statement directly verifies diesel dependence since August 20 and localized weekend ceasefire for power-line repairs. Work expected to finish is not restored off-site electricity. New September 8 strike tallies remain attributed/index-only; hold.

reports.headline: AP verifies Kfar Rumman toll; existing truce violation reinforced
reports.text: AP full report via PBS verifies September 7 Kfar Rumman strikes: Health Ministry reports at least 12 killed, including two children. Israeli military attributes strikes to drone attacks; Hezbollah did not claim them. Existing truce-violation evidence strengthened, not a new numerical increment; prisoner exchange remains prior context.

reports.headline: Fresh piracy reporting describes earlier hijackings
reports.text: September 8 Guardian original full article retrieved by terminal HTTP and Responsible Statecraft analysis document piracy resurgence and earlier April-August hijackings. Fresh structural reporting, not a separately established September 8 seizure; hold and monitor maritime incident notices.

reports.headline: Destroyer commissioning is not a new weapons test
reports.text: Reuters full text confirms Kang Kon commissioning occurred Sunday September 6. Kim calls it part of nuclear response system but KCNA does not establish nuclear weapons aboard. Official DVIDS confirms allied Freedom Edge opening September 7. Neither is a newly verified DPRK missile-range or nuclear test; hold.

reports.headline: Sabotage arrests relate to August energy-site attacks
reports.text: September 7 Turkiye Today full text says GNU announced September 6 arrests of five suspects over attacks in first half of August. New investigation reporting, not a fresh refinery strike; hold. Broader index adds UN roadmap and French engagement coverage.

reports.headline: Quintet mission scheduled to begin; no outcome confirmed
reports.text: Official EEAS confirms planned September 8-10 AU/IGAD/Arab League/EU/UN consultations in Khartoum. UN September 7 civilian-harm warning appears in past-day index. No completed mission or ceasefire established; hold.

reports.headline: Oil near $97 reflects supply risk, not nuclear odds
reports.text: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

reports.headline: Iran UN-referral push remains a draft, not an adopted decision
reports.text: September 8 Al Jazeera/Reuters says E3 and US seek support for referral; draft not formally submitted and wording remains unsettled. Baghaei threatens unspecified necessary measures. Continuing inspection gap corroborated; no newly verified enrichment measurement or nuclear test.

reports.headline: Manila reports unchanged US commitments despite regional drill concerns
reports.text: September 7 Reuters interview, retrieved via AsiaOne, quotes Teodoro warning China may exploit gaps but reporting definite US treaty assurances and no reduction in US-Philippine military activities. This is an allied-position update, not an observed new clash.

reports.headline: Reuters corroborates Norway warning; launcher delivery was in August
reports.text: September 7 Reuters confirms Moscow warning over US missile launchers, strategic-dialogue criticism and conditional wartime targeting. Delivery predates the statement. No observed nuclear alert change or explicit nuclear-use threat is established.

reports.headline: Myanmar corridor fighting warrants follow-up; full detail unavailable
reports.text: September 8 Nikkei headline and opening material report intensified operations around Chinese economic-corridor projects and civilian displacement. Full operational details not retrieved, so new publication is not assigned as new offensive onset. Hold score pending corroboration.

reports.headline: New Haiti analysis highlights rural gang expansion, not a new-day massacre
reports.text: September 7 Reuters full text cites GI-TOC findings on mobile rural raids, roadblocks, kidnappings and worsening Artibonite insecurity. Kenscoff is a recent example; exact attack onset is not established as today. Structural warning strengthened without automatic probability increment.

reports.headline: Official release confirms Freedom Edge has begun
reports.text: DVIDS confirms September 7 opening with Japan, Republic of Korea and United States; runs September 7-11. This resolves prior index-only start confirmation, not evidence of a DPRK weapons test.

reports.headline: Mandera reports separated: September 6 assault versus July recirculation
reports.text: Direct Kenyans.co.ke article 126850 dates Arabia Town attack to September 6, casualties unconfirmed. Article 125576 recirculating in September concerns July Fino/Arabia attacks, explicitly distinguished by newer article and July 25 Xinhua. Newer assault is not verified fresh mobilization or infrastructure-strike signal. Hold; correct source dating.

reports.headline: IAEA: verification gap persists; Gulf radiation remains at background levels
reports.text: September 7 IAEA full statement verifies no information or facility access in reporting period and lost inventory continuity for over a year. This supports existing access-denial assessment, not a verified new 90% enrichment or nuclear test. Gulf radiation reported at normal background levels. Hold.

reports.headline: Hormuz corridor remains proposed; shipping has not stopped
reports.text: September 7 Reuters full text confirms proposed restricted zone/corridor, not implementation or zero traffic. Ten commodity transits daily on ten-day average; US energy secretary separately claims flows recovering. Weekend tanker strikes and conditional retaliation remain prior-window context. No new minefield or bomber deployment independently verified; hold.

reports.headline: Qalibaf warns US-linked Gulf energy assets are exposed
reports.text: September 7 Yeni Safak, citing Anadolu and Qalibaf, reports a conditional warning against US-linked Gulf oil and gas assets if Iranian assets are struck. This corroborates the existing energy threat, not an observed new facility attack. Later Reuters headline indexed; full article unavailable.

reports.headline: CPJ documents journalist injuries across Lebanon and Gaza
reports.text: CPJ reports two Lebanese journalists and a Gaza journalist injured on September 6; another Gaza injury was two weeks earlier. September 7 publication is new corroborating reporting, not four new-day injuries or a separate probability increment.

reports.headline: UN rights warning highlights expanding drone harm
reports.text: Radio Tamazuj reports September 7 UN rights calls to halt fighting and foreign involvement, with rising civilian danger across Kordofan, Blue Nile and Darfur. Casualty examples in the report are not established as new-day attacks. Quintet September 8-10 mission remains prospective.

reports.headline: Haiti rural-expansion reporting traced to September 4 analysis
reports.text: Fresh Reuters-indexed coverage points to a structural shift outside Port-au-Prince. Original GI-TOC analysis is dated September 4 and describes the August 23 Kenscoff attack. Do not count the recirculated massacre as a fresh September event.
sources: Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime

reports.headline: Quintet confirms September 8–10 Khartoum political mission
reports.text: New official EEAS Quintet statement confirms planned September 8–10 Khartoum good-offices mission with AU, IGAD, Arab League, EU and UN; coordination with Quad. Scheduled political consultations, not an agreed ceasefire or completed mission. No numerical change.

reports.headline: Norway launcher warning corroborated; no verified nuclear alert
reports.text: September 7 AeroTime full report and Anadolu search corroborate attributed Russian warning that Norway launcher infrastructure is a wartime target and undermines strategic dialogue. Russian official page extraction failed; secondary sources retained. August 27 launcher delivery is not a new deployment today; no explicit nuclear-use threat or fresh alert verified. Hold.

reports.headline: Gaza ministry reports five killed in preceding 24 hours
reports.text: Direct September 7 Al Jazeera reports Gaza ministry tally of five killed and thirty injured over preceding 24 hours, with two further deaths from earlier wounds. Dates span September 6–7; attributed casualty reporting, no independently isolated additional operational threshold. Hold inherited score, not calm.

reports.headline: Full IAEA statement verifies continuing Iran safeguards access gap
reports.text: The September 7 prepared Board statement says the Agency received neither facility-status information nor in-field access in the reporting period. It lost continuity of knowledge of previously declared uranium inventories up to 60% over a year ago. This resolves the earlier full-source access gap; it does not establish new enrichment, a weapon or an adopted referral.

reports.headline: IAEA: repair ceasefire underway; grid restoration not yet confirmed
reports.text: Grossi says the seventh local arrangement took hold over the weekend, allowing demining and line repairs. Emergency diesel has powered the site since August 20; cooling pumps operated intermittently as fuel depleted. Repairs expected shortly is not confirmation of restored electricity.

reports.headline: Lebanon toll updated to 12 in AFP report
reports.text: AFP now cites the Lebanese health ministry reporting 11 killed in one Kfar Rumman building strike and a rescuer killed in another attack. Earlier Reuters reporting gave at least 11. This updates the same overnight violence, not a separate score increment.

reports.headline: Nigeria truce investigation concerns June-origin arrangement
reports.text: The New Humanitarian reports a Boko Haram truce operating since June and possible extension, based on three contacts. Government and military did not respond before publication; ISWAP is excluded. New reporting does not establish a newly signed nationwide settlement. Await corroboration; score held.

reports.headline: Russia warns over Norway launcher; deployment predates today
reports.text: AeroTime attributes a September 7 wartime-target warning to Zakharova. The launcher arrived August 27 for an exercise ending September 4; published US material does not specify accompanying munitions. No explicit nuclear-use threat or changed nuclear alert is established here.
sources: AeroTime citing Russian statements and US/Norwegian releases

reports.headline: IAEA resolves Syria past-nuclear safeguards questions
reports.text: Grossi reports that Syrian information and access allowed outstanding past-nuclear safeguards issues to be clarified and resolved. This is national safeguards progress, not proof of Idlib battlefield de-escalation; the existing regional tracker is held.

reports.headline: Fresh Grossi access headlines await full-statement verification

reports.headline: Mandera date mismatch: direct article says Friday, not Monday dawn
reports.text: A September 7 indexed attack headline led to a direct article describing Friday evening attacks in Fino and Arabia. A social post instead says Monday dawn. Event date is unresolved; do not count a fresh Monday attack.

reports.headline: Kang Kon commissioning is not a newly verified missile or nuclear test
reports.text: Reuters reports the warship was formally deployed September 6 and Kim described a nuclear response role. Actual weapons aboard were unspecified. The current configured test signals are not established by commissioning alone.

reports.headline: Manila pairs alliance-gap warning with US security assurances
reports.text: Teodoro warns China could exploit reduced US-South Korean drills, but reports definite US commitments to Manila. Freedom Edge trilateral drills are scheduled September 7-11; Seoul has not decided on a Hormuz deployment.

reports.headline: Reuters reports at least 11 killed in overnight Kfar Rumman strikes
reports.text: Reuters September 7 cites Lebanon's NNA: overnight building and vehicle strikes killed at least 11, including two children and two medics. Separate from Sunday's toll. Existing truce-violation assessment corroborated; no score increase.

reports.headline: Iran outlines proposed Gulf restricted zone; implementation not verified
reports.text: Reuters September 7 reports future restricted-zone and corridor maps, with signature expected in coming days. Kpler records ten daily commodity transits on a ten-day average. Severe disruption is not zero traffic.

reports.headline: Event-date check: Kenscoff 47-death attack occurred in August
reports.text: Past-day index recirculates a 47-death Haiti headline. Direct August 27 Al Jazeera/AP coverage dates the mass kidnapping and attack to August 23. Not counted as a newly verified September massacre.

reports.headline: Niger mutiny review distinguishes allegation from verified intervention
reports.text: September 6 Al Jazeera/Reuters review dates the failed mutiny to August 29. Niger alleges French orchestration; France denies it. No newly established French military intervention and no duplicate theatre added.

reports.headline: Hormuz traffic at lowest since May, but not zero
reports.text: Reuters' September 7 dateline cites Kpler: ten commodity ships per day on a ten-day average; two passed Saturday and six Sunday. No VLCC had exited since Wednesday. This strengthens evidence of severe shipping disruption without establishing a complete closure.
sources: Reuters citing Kpler, LSEG and UKMTO

reports.headline: Manila warns of alliance gaps; US assurances remain
reports.text: September 7 Al Jazeera/AP/Reuters reports Teodoro's warning that China may exploit reduced US-South Korean exercises. He also cites definite US assurances to Manila. Five-day Freedom Edge drills are due to begin today; South Korean Hormuz contributions remain undecided.

reports.headline: Libya announces arrests over older energy-facility attacks
reports.text: Anadolu reports the unity government's Sunday announcement that five suspects were arrested. The article explicitly dates the underlying drone attacks to early August. This is a new investigative announcement, not a newly verified attack.
sources: Anadolu citing Government of National Unity

reports.headline: Kang Kon joins fleet; actual nuclear load unspecified
reports.text: Reuters confirms Sunday's commissioning and Kim's description of the destroyer as part of a nuclear response system. The report does not specify nuclear weapons aboard. No qualifying new test is established; score held.
sources: Reuters via SRN News, citing KCNA

reports.headline: UN confirms September 8 Quintet meetings; no Monday briefing
reports.text: The browser-verified September 4 UN briefing schedules envoy and Quintet meetings in Khartoum for September 8. It also says there will be no September 7 noon briefing because of Labor Day. These are scheduled contacts, not a signed settlement.

reports.headline: Reuters confirms Sunday destroyer commissioning and nuclear-role rhetoric
reports.text: Reuters, citing KCNA, dates Kang Kon commissioning to September 6. Kim describes a nuclear-response role, but nuclear weapons aboard are unspecified. US, South Korea and Japan begin Freedom Edge on September 7. Neither configured test trigger is established; score held.
sources: Reuters via WMBD; KCNA and South Korean JCS attributed

reports.headline: AP corroborates planned exclusion zone; implementation unverified
reports.text: AP September 6 directly corroborates Rezaei's planned exclusion-zone announcement. Coordinates and implementation remain unclear, and the US denies the claimed vessel hit. Attributed oil-transit estimates conflict with tracking averages; no confirmed zero traffic.

reports.headline: OPEC directly confirms October production hold
reports.text: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

reports.headline: Taiwan patrol investigation describes a campaign dating to June
reports.text: Direct Bloomberg syndication reports east-coast patrols averaging two cutters monthly since June. Taiwan coast guard response and US criticism are included. The September publication does not establish a new blockade or invasion; hold without double-counting in South China Sea.

reports.headline: Envoys cite progress, but no settlement; plant power remains critical
reports.text: September 6 Kyiv Post reports US envoys seeking renewed trilateral talks after meetings with Zelensky and European advisers. IAEA Update 365 confirms repair arrangements but continued diesel and cooling vulnerability. Diplomatic progress claims are not a signed peace deal; nuclear safety is distinct from weapons use.

reports.headline: AFP confirms rising days-long Yemen toll and displacement
reports.text: AFP September 6 reports more than 300 combatants and some civilians killed in days of fighting, with journalists observing displaced families. A reported Taiz-Mokha road cutoff increases maritime-access concern but does not prove complete strait closure. Existing score held.

reports.headline: Iran announces planned maritime restriction beyond Hormuz
reports.text: Anadolu reports Rezaei says a restricted zone will be declared in coming days and an Oman corridor agreement is planned. His complete-closure and missile-test claims are unverified; announcement is not implementation. No new closure signal.

reports.headline: New Deir al-Zahrani evacuation warning follows deadly Sunday strikes
reports.text: Anadolu reports an early-Monday Israeli warning before a planned strike in Deir al-Zahrani. Reuters separately confirms seven killed Sunday, citing Lebanon's health ministry. Warning is not confirmation of a completed strike; existing ceasefire-violation signal held.

reports.headline: Yemen fighting toll exceeds 300; government reports tanker interception
reports.text: AFP reports more than 300 combatants and some civilians killed over several days, with displacement witnessed by its journalists. Anadolu relays a Coast Guard account that tanker Nerida was intercepted after a Ras Isa delivery and gunfire; no casualties reported. No verified strait closure; score held.

reports.headline: Kyiv talks include allied consultation; nuclear-plant power remains key trigger
reports.text: Anadolu confirms September 6 talks with US envoys; Ukrainian side says British, French and German advisers join expanded format. No peace agreement verified. IAEA Update 365 warns dwindling diesel and intermittent cooling make off-site power restoration urgent, a nuclear-safety risk rather than weapons-use evidence.

reports.headline: Libya announces sabotage-cell arrests linked to August attacks
reports.text: Anadolu relays GNU announcement of five arrests over drone attacks on Tripoli and Zawiya energy facilities. The cited attacks occurred in the first half of August. New arrest statement is not a new infrastructure strike; hold.

reports.headline: Iranian Erbil aerostat claim refers to an earlier strike
reports.text: Anadolu reports IRGC claims an aerostat was destroyed near Erbil during Wednesday's clashes; no immediate US comment. September 6 publication does not make this a new attack. Uncorroborated claim held below activation threshold.

reports.headline: Lebanon death toll rises to seven; Aoun seeks US intervention
reports.text: September 6 AFP via Dawn updates the death toll to at least seven, citing Lebanon's health ministry, including three in a separate Nabatieh al-Tahta drone strike. Aoun appeals for US intervention. Existing ceasefire violation persists; hold saturated score.

reports.headline: Wright downplays nuclear-deal prospects; referral remains proposed
reports.text: AP and direct draft-resolution reporting confirm US/E3 referral effort, not adopted UN action. September 6 Wright interview reporting downplays prospects for a signed deal; pessimism is not an explicit new refusal. No fresh verified weapons-grade enrichment or nuclear test; hold.

reports.headline: US disputes Iranian vessel-hit claim; oil transit estimates remain contested
reports.text: AP September 6 confirms US denial of an alleged unmanned-vessel hit and US acknowledgment of September 5 tanker strikes. Wright's 9 million barrels/day transit figure is attributed and exceeds longer-period tracking estimates. No verified total closure or zero traffic; hold.

reports.headline: Kyiv diplomacy continues alongside critical nuclear-plant power risk
reports.text: Reuters photo caption and DW/agency reporting corroborate September 6 Kyiv visit by US envoys; European advisers reportedly participate. No settlement verified. IAEA Update 365 directly confirms repair ceasefire and diesel/cooling vulnerability; nuclear safety is not weapons use. Hold.

reports.headline: Somalia issues piracy warning; cited rescue dates to August 29
reports.text: Eastleigh Voice September 6 directly reports Somali government piracy warning and international-cooperation appeal. Incidents date from April; MV Lutuf liberation dated August 29. New statement is not a new hijacking. Hold; no signal change.

reports.headline: Reuters reports US envoys met Zelenskyy; no settlement confirmed
reports.text: September 6 Reuters search snippet reports envoys met Zelenskyy in Kyiv, corroborated by BBC news index; full Reuters syndication timed out. Existing diplomacy_active held, no peace deal confirmed. IAEA Update 365 directly confirms repair ceasefire and critical diesel/off-site-power risk, not weapons use.
sources: Reuters search excerpt; BBC news index

reports.headline: AP: US denies vessel-hit claim; oil-flow estimate remains attributed
reports.text: AP September 6 directly confirms US denial of the alleged unmanned-vessel hit and acknowledged September 5 tanker strikes. Wright estimates 9 million barrels/day transit; AP notes estimate exceeds tracking averages. No verified zero traffic or total closure. Hold.

reports.headline: Lebanon reports four killed in dawn strikes; pullback not approved
reports.text: September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP directly reports at least four killed and 20 wounded, citing Lebanese authorities; Israel attributes strikes to Hezbollah drones. Qatar urges de-escalation. Pullback plan remains unapproved. Hold.

reports.headline: US rejects Iran claim of a vessel hit; damage remains unverified
reports.text: AP September 6 confirms the US explicitly denies Iran's claimed hit on an unmanned vessel. September 5 US tanker strikes remain acknowledged. Wright's ABC interview reports substantial but restricted oil transit; no verified zero traffic or total Hormuz closure. Hold.

reports.headline: Wright says nuclear agreement may not happen; no technical threshold verified
reports.text: September 6 ABC transcript: Wright says a nuclear agreement may not occur and emphasizes destroying capabilities. This is a policy statement, not confirmed enrichment, weapons development or a formal refusal of talks. IAEA confirms regular Board meeting September 7; US/E3 referral effort is not adopted action. Hold.

reports.headline: IAEA regular Board opens September 7; agenda is not a resolution
reports.text: IAEA schedules Board opening at 10:00 CEST September 7 and Grossi press conference at 12:30 CEST. Iran, DPRK and Ukraine are on the agenda. This is a regular scheduled meeting, not evidence of emergency action or an adopted Iran referral.

reports.headline: US envoys reach Ukraine; ZNPP repair and diesel risk remain unresolved
reports.text: ABC September 6 directly reports US envoys arriving in Ukraine after Moscow talks; no settlement confirmed. IAEA Update 365 confirms local repair ceasefire, off-site power loss and dwindling diesel at ZNPP. Safety risk is distinct from nuclear-weapons use. Hold.

reports.headline: Lebanon dawn strikes confirmed; proposed pullback not approved
reports.text: Direct September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP report corroborates dawn strikes and at least four deaths attributed to Lebanese authorities. Qatar presses de-escalation. Proposed Israeli pullback is unapproved, not an implemented withdrawal. Existing ceasefire_violation corroborated; hold.

reports.text: Direct September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP confirms intense western-front fighting and OCHA displacement. Hais recapture is a government claim, not independently verified control. No verified Bab al-Mandab closure. Hold saturated score.

reports.text: Reuters September 5 directly confirms US NATO envoy backs primarily national responses to hybrid attacks. Antisubmarine-exercise headlines do not establish weapons alert or Article 5. Hold.

reports.text: ABC transcript quotes Wright putting seven-day Hormuz oil transit slightly above 9 million barrels/day, or 13-14 million including bypass pipelines. reports.headline: Fresh Lebanon strikes corroborated in September 6 report
reports.text: September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP direct report verifies fresh dawn strikes; NNA and Health Ministry report at least four killed. Israel attributes response to Hezbollah drones. Existing ceasefire_violation corroborated; hold saturated score.

reports.text: Direct draft-resolution report confirms US/E3 referral proposal, not adopted Board or Security Council action. No fresh enrichment or nuclear-test threshold verified. Hold.

reports.text: IAEA Update 365 directly confirms repair ceasefire and continuing ZNPP diesel/cooling risk. September 6 BBC/NBC news indexes report US envoys arriving in Kyiv; no settlement verified. Nuclear safety is distinct from weapons use. Hold.

reports.text: September 6 Al Jazeera/AFP confirms continuing Taiz/Hodeidah fighting and reports OCHA displacement. Hais recapture remains government claim; no verified Bab al-Mandab closure. Existing ceasefire_violation corroborated; hold.

reports.text: Reuters September 5 NATO envoy remarks support primarily national responses to hybrid attacks. Official NATO assistance page is July background, not a fresh deployment or nuclear alert. Hold.

reports.text: IAEA Update 365 directly confirms local repair ceasefire, off-site power loss and diesel scarcity at ZNPP. Reuters reports Moscow talks without announced breakthrough. Nuclear-safety risk is not nuclear-weapons use. Hold.

reports.text: Direct Al Jazeera/AFP September 6 report confirms ongoing western-front fighting and reports civilian displacement. Hais recapture remains a Yemeni military claim; no verified Bab al-Mandab closure. Hold saturated score.

reports.text: Kenya Ministry of Defence confirms continuing AU peace-process engagement and a recent Mekelle visit but does not date the visit. Similar Reporter story is June 11, not September 5. Positive context, not a verified new timed signal; hold.

reports.text: Direct Anadolu report dates suspected Tripoli depot drone to September 3; operator reported no injuries and normal fuel operations. September 5 republication is not a new attack. Hold.

reports.text: US/E3 referral draft remains a proposal, not adopted IAEA or Security Council action. No newly verified enrichment, weaponization or test threshold. Access restriction carried; hold.

reports.text: IAEA Update 365 confirms repairs to the 330 kV line have started after demining. Off-site power has been absent since August 20; emergency generation and intermittent cooling continue. A station blackout is possible within days unless power or diesel delivery is restored. Nuclear-safety risk, not nuclear-weapons use.

reports.headline: Iran referral still a draft before regular Board meeting
reports.text: AP draft text and official IAEA calendar reviewed: E3/US referral remains unsubmitted proposal, not adopted action. Access restrictions persist per AP report; no freshly verified weapon or enrichment threshold. Hold.

reports.headline: US acknowledgment of tanker strikes remains central risk
reports.text: AP confirms US military acknowledgment of three tanker strikes and oil-fleet threat September 5. Later reciprocal-attack headlines remain attributed; no verified total traffic cessation. Hold.

reports.text: Narinjara direct HTTP fallback reports September 4 Ponnagyun pagoda bombardment, published September 5, citing locals. Single-source and outside event window; do not re-date or inflate. Hold.

reports.text: Direct report confirms US/UK/France/Germany draft referral proposal, not adoption. Official IAEA index confirms regular September 7-11 Board meeting. No fresh enrichment/test threshold; access-denial signal carried, not independently reconfirmed today.

reports.text: AP direct report confirms CENTCOM acknowledged three tanker strikes and threatened the oil fleet September 5. Damage and attack sequence remain military claims; later retaliation damage unverified. Hold.

reports.text: Al Jazeera September 5 full report describes government air attacks and continued western-front fighting; reinforcement and territorial claims attributed/contested. Existing truce-breach signal reconfirmed; effective Bab al-Mandeb closure not verified. Hold.

reports.text: Reuters September 5 confirms US NATO envoy support for national responses to hybrid attacks; submarine-defence reporting does not establish nuclear alert or Article 5 decision. Hold.

reports.text: AP and Reuters September 5 attribute three tanker strikes to CENTCOM following alleged missile attacks on US warships. Oil-fleet threat reconfirmed. Late Iranian retaliation headlines await independent damage verification; no new signal.

reports.headline: Capital-specific restraint is not a nationwide Ukraine ceasefire
reports.text: Al Jazeera/AFP September 5 confirms Moscow talks and capital-specific three-day strike restraint, with Kyiv visit expected September 6. Reuters late headline says useful talks without breakthrough; body not retrieved. Not a nationwide ceasefire.

reports.headline: IAEA Board meets September 7-11; referral not yet adopted
reports.text: IAEA official index confirms regular September 7-11 Board meeting. Referral draft remains a proposal, not adoption. No newly verified enrichment or test threshold; existing access-denial signal carried, not freshly verified.

reports.headline: Yemen offensive threatens approaches, not verified strait closure
reports.text: Al Jazeera September 5 describes government air attacks and Houthi push toward al-Makha/Bab al-Mandeb. Territorial gains and casualty totals attributed/contested. Truce-breach signal reconfirmed; no verified effective strait closure.

reports.headline: Ali al-Taher control remains an Israeli claim
reports.text: Al Jazeera September 5 details Israeli claim of operational control of Ali al-Taher ridge; extent remains uncertain. A proposed wider buffer zone is not a verified new deployment. Hold. reports.headline: NATO hybrid warning does not establish nuclear alert
reports.text: Reuters confirms US NATO envoy support for national responses to hybrid attacks. Submarine-defence exercise reporting is not evidence of a nuclear alert or nuclear-use threat.

reports.text: AP full report: Putin met Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow September 5; Kyiv visit planned Sunday. Both sides agreed to a limited pause on strikes against the two capitals through Monday, not a nationwide ceasefire. Existing diplomatic signal reconfirmed. Hold.

reports.headline: Government air operations intensify near Red Sea approaches
reports.text: Al Jazeera September 5 full report describes government air attacks September 4 and continued Houthi offensive toward al-Makha and Bab al-Mandeb. Counts and casualties are attributed; territorial gains contested. Existing truce-breach signal reconfirmed; no proof of strait closure. Hold.

reports.headline: Tanker strikes and oil-fleet warning remain central risk
reports.text: AP full report confirms CENTCOM says it struck three Iranian tankers and threatened the oil fleet after alleged missile attacks on US warships. Already reflected in prior scan; damage and sequence remain military claims. Hold.

reports.headline: IAEA confirms September 7-11 Board meeting; referral remains proposal
reports.text: Official IAEA advisory confirms regular Board meeting September 7-11. AP indexed September 4 report describes a proposed Iran referral resolution, not adoption. Reuters September 1 extraction lacks article body. No new technical threshold verified. Hold.

reports.headline: NATO envoy stresses national responses to hybrid threats
reports.text: Reuters full report quotes US NATO envoy on national responses to hybrid attacks and protection of critical infrastructure. Submarine-defence headlines do not establish a nuclear alert. Hold.

reports.text: Reuters confirms Vietnam-Myanmar agreement on training, exchanges, rescue and security cooperation. Not verified new combat materiel or battlefield support delivery. Hold.

reports.text: AP and Reuters on September 5 report CENTCOM acknowledging strikes on three Iranian tankers after missile attacks on US warships. AP quotes an explicit threat to destroy the oil fleet. Activate oil_infrastructure_threat; retain capped score. Damage and attack sequence are attributed to CENTCOM, not independently inspected. Supersedes earlier unconfirmed-only assessment.

reports.headline: US NATO envoy warns against hybrid attacks; response remains primarily national
reports.text: Reuters September 5 quotes US NATO envoy warning against hybrid attacks and supporting national responses. This is not a verified new nuclear threat or Article 5 decision; hold.

reports.headline: Vietnam-Myanmar defence cooperation agreement: implementation remains the watch point
reports.text: Reuters September 5 confirms Vietnam agreement on training, officer exchanges, search-and-rescue and security cooperation. No weapons delivery or combat support verified; monitor implementation; the agreement alone does not justify a signal activation.

reports.headline: Explosions reported near Kharg Island; tanker-strike claim remains unconfirmed
reports.text: Iranian media reported several explosions near Kharg Island, Iran's main Gulf petroleum-export hub. Fars reported blasts without visible smoke; SNN alleged a U.S. strike on an Iranian tanker. Neither U.S. nor Iranian officials had confirmed the claim. The report keeps the site on immediate watch but is insufficient for a new indicator or probability move; Iran conventional holds 100/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: IAEA-brokered local halt enables urgent Zaporizhzhia power-line repairs
reports.text: A localized safety pause took effect around the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant so Ukrainian technicians could restore external power after demining. The plant had relied on emergency diesel generators since August 20, with the IAEA warning that fuel reserves were running low. The step lowers immediate station-blackout risk but is local and temporary, not a theater-wide settlement; Russia-Ukraine holds 99/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: USS George Washington relieves long-deployed Lincoln in Middle East rotation
reports.text: The Associated Press reports USS George Washington arrived to relieve USS Abraham Lincoln while USS George H.W. Bush remains in the region. The rotation sustains a two-carrier U.S. posture and blockade capacity but replaces a long-deployed ship rather than proving a fresh net increase. Iran conventional remains capped at 100/IMMINENT; the unusual concentration stays on watch.

reports.headline: Israel and Hezbollah remain in daily combat over strategic Ali Taher ridge
reports.text: The Associated Press reports that Israel says it has taken operational control of the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon after weeks of daily shelling and airstrikes, while Hezbollah has repeatedly attacked Israeli forces there with drones. The extent of Israeli control is unclear and Hezbollah had not issued an official response. The report independently strengthens the existing kinetic-breach picture but does not create a new canonical indicator; ceasefire_violation is reconfirmed and risk holds 99 raw / 100 coupled, IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Hormuz normalization odds remain near floor in morning market check
reports.text: Polymarket displayed a 3% chance of Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by September 30 and 1% by September 15, while the weekly 20-39-transit bracket was priced at 79%. Definitions and horizons differ from DoomsdayWatch, so this is a market sanity check only: no signal or probability change.

reports.headline: Niger blames France for failed mutiny; allegation remains unsubstantiated
reports.text: Reuters reports Niger's government accused France of inciting the August 29 attack on the airport, military base and presidency. Niger said it had assembled evidence but made none public; the army, backed by Russian paramilitary forces, regained control the next day. The episode remains mapped to the existing Central Sahel tracker and does not establish a new sustained escalation threshold; Mali-Sahel holds 40/CRITICAL.

reports.headline: Trump signals possible halt to U.S. allied arms sales over Ukraine costs
reports.text: Reuters reports that President Trump said European states should repay the United States for arms and munitions previously sent to Ukraine and appeared to signal a halt in future sales to allied nations. This is a material alliance-cohesion watch item, but no NATO collective-defence decision, direct NATO-Russia engagement or configured tracker transition was verified; Russia-Ukraine remains 99/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: U.S. envoys head to Russia and Ukraine to relaunch mediation
reports.text: Al Jazeera was indexed reporting that U.S. envoys are headed to Russia and Ukraine to relaunch mediation. This reconfirms the configured diplomacy_active indicator, but no mutually accepted ceasefire terms or halt in attacks was verified; Russia-Ukraine holds 99/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Oil ends week higher as renewed U.S.-Iran strikes push diesel to a record
reports.text: Reuters reported that oil finished the week higher and that diesel hit a record as renewed U.S.-Iran strikes disrupted supply. Only the headline was indexed and the article body could not be extracted directly, so this is treated as a market sanity check that corroborates elevated energy stress; it changes no probability and no indicator.

reports.headline: Hezbollah drone report and Israeli strikes keep Lebanon truce under pressure
reports.text: The Israeli military said a Hezbollah drone was launched toward its forces in southern Lebanon and that it subsequently struck Hezbollah infrastructure. The underlying claim is party-attributed and the two retrieved reports repeat the same military statement, but it adds another current-window kinetic-breach report. The existing truce-breach indicator is reconfirmed; no probability increase is possible at the coupled ceiling.

reports.headline: Trump says U.S. may hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain soon
reports.text: Reuters was indexed reporting President Trump said the United States may strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain soon. The explicit strike threat reinforces the absence of a durable off-ramp, but it does not establish a fresh configured force-deployment signal and Iran conventional risk is already capped at 100/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: US rejects Israeli ministers’ calls to remove Palestinians from Gaza
reports.text: Al Jazeera reports that U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff rejected suggestions by Israeli ministers that Palestinians be removed from Gaza. The public disagreement is an allied-position watch item; it does not by itself establish a ceasefire, implemented displacement order or new configured conflict signal.
sources: U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff (quoted by Al Jazeera)

reports.headline: US says active mediation is pressing for a humanitarian truce in Sudan
reports.text: A senior U.S. adviser said Washington is pressing, with Saudi Arabia and Egypt, for a humanitarian truce and unhindered aid access, and that negotiations are continuing. This activates sudan:diplomacy_active as a formal mediation effort; neither SAF nor RSF acceptance is verified, so the conflict probability remains 100.
sources: U.S. Senior Adviser for Arab and African Affairs (quoted by Anadolu)

reports.headline: Israeli drone strike kills two in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
reports.text: Lebanon's Health Ministry said an Israeli drone hit a vehicle in Wadi Barghaz, killing two people, after strikes and shelling across several southern towns. Anadolu and Middle East Eye reported the deaths. The fresh strikes despite ceasefire reconfirm the existing ceasefire_violation indicator; no separate probability increase is justified because the tracker is already capped after coupling.

reports.headline: US envoys due in Kyiv after Moscow talks as negotiations remain active
reports.text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected in Kyiv after CIA Director John Ratcliffe met Vladimir Putin in Moscow and conveyed a proposal. The engagement activates russia_ukraine:diplomacy_active, but Kyiv says core territory and security-guarantee disputes remain unresolved and no ceasefire exists; probability is held.

reports.headline: Yemen fighting intensifies near Taiz and the Bab al-Mandeb approach
reports.text: Yemeni government forces said they retook two hills west of Taiz after a broad Houthi offensive across western Taiz and southern Hodeidah. Al Jazeera reported more than 100 fighters killed across both sides and an apparent Houthi push toward al-Makha and heights overlooking Bab al-Mandeb. Reporting is party-attributed and casualty totals vary, but the kinetic picture remains acute; Yemen-Red Sea holds 100/IMMINENT.

reports.headline: Iranian army says doctrine is shifting toward preemptive attack
reports.text: Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia told IRNA that Iran is moving from reactive defence toward preemptive operations and expanded long-range strike capability. The statement hardens conventional posture but does not map cleanly to a configured canonical signal; no synthetic signal or probability increment was added.

reports.headline: Hormuz traffic remains far below normal as U.S. and Iran trade strikes
reports.text: USNI News reported that the United States carried out renewed strikes on Iranian targets and on two vessels while Iranian attacks on commercial shipping continued. Forty-four U.S.-facilitated transits of the Strait of Hormuz were recorded across 1-2 September, against a pre-war average of about 138 per day, and the Joint Maritime Information Center warned that uncharted or drifting mines may be present. Traffic through the strait is severely restricted but remains non-zero, mine risk persists, and no total closure was verified.

reports.headline: Finland investigates possible territorial violation after drone found on southern coast
reports.text: Reuters reports that Finnish authorities are investigating whether national territory was violated after a drone was found on the southern coast. No origin, hostile attribution, casualties, damage or NATO Article 4/5 action was verified. This remains an alliance-watch item and does not activate a configured Russia tracker signal.

reports.headline: Western powers seek IAEA board referral of Iran to UN Security Council
reports.text: Reuters reports that the United States, Britain, France and Germany are lobbying the IAEA’s 35-nation board to pass a resolution next week referring Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years. The proposed step follows unresolved stockpile declarations and access demands. This reconfirms the existing safeguards-access restriction; the Board has not yet passed the resolution, so no emergency-board-action threshold is scored.

reports.headline: Pacific summit records concern over Chinese missile test without a fresh launch threshold
reports.text: Reuters reports that Pacific leaders backed concerns over a Chinese missile test despite Nauru dissent. The retrieved report reflects a regional diplomatic-position statement; it did not establish a new launch, Taiwan blockade or other configured China or South China Sea indicator inside this scan window.
sources: Pacific Islands Forum communiqué (reported by Reuters)

reports.headline: Four Lebanese detainees released in Red Cross-mediated handover
reports.text: Lebanon said four detainees were returned from Israel through an ICRC-mediated transfer. Anadolu and Al Jazeera reported the handover. This reconfirms the existing diplomacy_active indicator but does not outweigh continued combat or Hezbollah rejection of the broader arrangement.
sources: International Committee of the Red Cross

reports.headline: U.S. political pressure favors containing the Iran fight, but strike options remain open
reports.text: Al Jazeera reports that U.S. advisers have strong electoral incentives to avoid a return to full-scale war before the November midterms, while Vice President Vance said economic, military, diplomatic and covert pressure all remain available. This is analysis of restraint incentives, not a formal negotiating round or verified ceasefire; no canonical signal or probability changes.

reports.headline: AP confirms Iran fired missiles and drones at Kuwait after U.S. strikes
reports.text: The Associated Press reports that Kuwait's air defenses intercepted Iranian missile and drone attacks on 3 September, after Bahrain and Jordan intercepted Iranian attacks the previous day. AP links the exchange to U.S. strikes on Iranian launchers that Washington said were intended to put mines into the Strait of Hormuz. This directly reconfirms the live U.S.-Iran strike cycle and restricted-Hormuz context, but does not establish total closure or zero traffic; probabilities remain unchanged.

reports.headline: NATO support posture holds without new collective-defence action
reports.text: NATO’s official posture remains support for Ukraine without direct alliance combat against Russia. This scan verified no new Article 4 or Article 5 decision and no new NATO combat deployment.

reports.headline: Prediction markets remain low on Taiwan invasion and NATO Article 5
